notes: Upstream-clone debugging task in sympy/sympy (issue #28744, fix f1b4be1b on parent 648f6cfb): in Mod.number_eval, the non-mod factor list is rebuilt by iterating over ALL of p.args instead of the already-filtered non_mod_l, so a factor of p that is itself a Mod expression is duplicated into both lists and the inner residue ends up squared whenever every factor reports is_integer (i.e. once a symbol carries an integer/even assumption) and the inner modulus differs from the outer one. The agent gets the real tree at the parent commit (single-object clone: git init + one depth-1 fetch of the pinned parent SHA; the fix commit is provably unreachable and never fetched), NO reproduction is handed to it - the instruction describes only the user-visible symptom and requires the agent to author /app/repro.sh (temporary pytest file planted in the owning package's test dir, run with the project's own runner, scrubbed on exit, exit 0 iff symptom absent) before fixing - then localise, fix, and verify against the project's own test tooling. Verifier: sha256 pins of the golden regression test (test_Mod from the fix commit's sympy/core/tests/test_arit.py, extracted at image build time into /opt/golden via a throwaway clone that is rm -rf'd, issue-number comment stripped so the image never leaks '#28744') and of the pristine pre-fix sympy/core/mod.py; provenance (HEAD == parent, fix commit unreachable, byte-level scope permitting ONLY sympy/core/mod.py to differ, no untracked non-ignored files); deliverables /app/repro.sh + /app/summary.md; the agent's repro run against the repaired tree copy (must exit 0) and against a copy with the pristine pre-fix mod.py restored (must exit non-zero); the golden test_Mod must PASS on the repaired tree and FAIL on the pre-fix copy; the whole of the project's own test_arit.py module with the regression test planted must pass (101 passed, 2 xfailed, ~17s at 1 CPU); three authored hidden cases (different moduli/coefficients 3/7/11, an even-assumption trigger 5/6/8, merged multiplier factors 2*Mod(t,4)*3 mod 9) each required to PASS on the repaired tree and FAIL on the pre-fix copy - all directions verified empirically in the task image at build time. Dependency pins: pytest==9.1.1, hypothesis==6.168.0, mpmath==1.3.0, Python 3.12 (bench-base:python-3.12); both-direction re-confirmation with these pins runs in the Dockerfile and fails the build if either direction regresses. Measured build ~90s, image ~740MB total. Trials run with the sandbox's default network policy (egress available), so the instruction never names the issue number, the fix commit, the fix content or the file: an agent that looks the issue up must still find, fix, and re-verify the bug in a real tree, and a grafted/fetched fix fails the provenance check. Difficulty lands medium (rubric 12): no reproduction provided, hidden multi-direction checks, exact-bytes scope, real upstream tree with a real test suite.
